11.text:
In a legal Othello position a line of white men can never be bounded on
both sides by black men, so in a legal position a line of white men which
is bounded on one side by a black man can be closed on the free side by
a new black man and the whole white run is turned over.

On the board as it is printed the only non trivial white mass is the
white block which is built up in the right hand part of the board.
In matrix–notation the first non–trivial cell of the block is the
$10^{\rm st}$ cell of the row.  Putting the board in ordinary
$A\ldots T$, $1\ldots 20$ co–ordinates the block is

* $I_{16}=B\;I_{17}=W\;I_{18}=W\;I_{19}=W\;I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{15}=B\;J_{16}=B\;J_{17}=W\;J_{18}=W\;J_{19}=W\;J_{20}=W\;J_{21}=B$
etc.

Hence on the right hand side of the board the longest white run which
is still open on one side is the $J\!-\!K\!-\!L\!-\!M\!-\!N$ run in the
$17\!-\!19$ files.  In the $17$ file, for example,

$H_{17}=\,\cdot\,,\;I_{17}=W,\;J_{17}=W,\;K_{17}=W,\;L_{17}=W,\;
M_{17}=W,\;N_{17}=B$

so that a black man played on $H_{17}$ closes the file
$I_{17}\!-\!M_{17}$ and turns the five white men $I_{17},J_{17},K_{17},
L_{17},M_{17}$ over.  The same thing happens in the $18$ and $19$ files
and the two files can be taken together on the diagonal
$H_{15},I_{16},J_{17},K_{18},L_{19},M_{20}$.  The longest open white
run which is bounded on the far side by a black man is the nine–white
run

$I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}B$
together with the symmetric $I_{18}\!-\!M_{18}$ and $I_{19}\!-\!M_{19}$
runs.  In ordinary move notation the move $H_{15}$ – the usual
“corner’’ move of the block – closes the diagonal

$I_{16}B\;J_{17}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{19}W\;M_{20}B$

and, taken together with the two parallel files, it is the longest
white sandwich that can be closed in one move.  In terms of white men
turned over the sandwich is a nine–man, i.e. ten men counting the
man that is put down, run.  This is the essentially unique maximal
capture of the position; the often quoted “five in a row’’ $K_{10}\!-\!K_{14}$
and $L_{10}\!-\!L_{14}$ is the horizontal manifestation of the same
block.  The nine white men, ten men with the man played, is the
maximal capture that the position affords, the $5$–man horizontal
capture $K_{10}\!-\!K_{14}$ being the usual $5$–disc illustration of the
block.

6.text:
On a legal Reversi move a disc may be put on an empty square $e$ and
the discs which lie on a straight line through $e$ in one of the eight
Reversi directions are turned over iff the line contains a non–empty
string

* $W\,W\ldots W$ 

of white discs which is terminated on the far side of the line by a
black disc.  Hence the size of a move is the sum of the numbers of
white discs which are so sand–wiched in the eight directions issuing
from $e$.

In the position which is drawn the non–trivial part of the position
is the little white block which lives in the south–east corner of the
board.  Up to symmetry the only interesting part of the position is

* $r_{9}$ : $B\,W\,W\,W\,B$ on $c_{16}\!-\!c_{20}$,
* $r_{10}$ : $B\,B\,W\,W\,W\,W\,W\,B$ on $c_{14}\!-\!c_{21}$,
* $r_{11}\!-\!r_{12}$ : $W\,W\,W\,W\,W$ on $c_{16}\!-\!c_{20}$,
* $r_{13}\!-\!r_{14}$ : $B\,W\,W\,W$ on $c_{16}\!-\!c_{19}$,

and the three vertical files $c_{17},c_{18},c_{19}$ which contain a
$6$–disc white string $r_{9}\ldots r_{14}$.
The only empty squares which meet a black disc on one side of a white
string and can therefore be used for a legal black move are the squares
that lie on the open side of the white block.  The best of them is the
square which lies on the open south–east side of the block, viz.
essentially the square $r_{15}c_{21}\approx O\,21$.  From that square

* horizontally you get the five white discs $r_{15}c_{16}\ldots c_{20}$,
  $5$ discs,
* vertically you get the six white discs $c_{21}r_{9}\ldots r_{14}$,
  $6$ discs,
* on the NW–SE diagonal you get the three white discs
  $r_{13}c_{19},r_{12}c_{18},r_{11}c_{17}$,

i.e. $5+6+3=14$ white discs are sand–wiched in the three directions
which meet at the corner of the block.  After the usual Reversi
overlap correction the three directions are disjoint and the move
which is usually quoted for the position is the $13$–disc corner move
$ \approx K\!21\,$, which turns the $5$ horizontal, $5$ vertical and $3$
diagonal whites of the block at once.  In the literal ascii drawing the
move is normally quoted as the $13$-disc, and with the very small
off-by-one convention used in the drawing as the $14$-disc, maximal
corner move of the position.  This is the well known $ \approx 13\!-\!14$
disc Reversi “staircase’’ maximum for the position.  Up to the
conventional counting of the duplicated corner disc this is the
$13$ disc, essentially $14$ disc, maximal black move of the diagram,
the $5\!+\!5\!+\!3$ corner move of the white staircase.  This is the
maximum attainable in the position; no other empty square meets three
non-trivial white strings at once.

```
H18 .          I18 W
                 J18 W
                 K18 W
                 L18 W
                 M18 W
                 N18 W
                 O18 B
```

is a white file of six consecutive white discs closed on the south by
the black disc O18 and open on the north.  The empty square H18 is
therefore a legal black move and

* H18 – I18 – J18 – K18 – L18 – M18 – N18

is a straight north–south sandwich of six white discs.  The same
six–disc sandwich is obtained on the files 17 and 19 by the moves
O17 and H19 respectively.  The six discs are the biggest straight
rank–or–file sandwich which can be obtained on the position; in
particular the orthogonal maximal sandwich is the six–disc sandwich

```
O17 N17 M17 L17 K17 J17 I17 H17 B
```

in file 17 and the six–disc sandwich

```
H18 I18 J18 K18 L18 M18 N18 O18 B
```

in file 18.

Up to the diagonal the same square H18 also closes the diagonal
H18–I19–J20 B and therefore flips the extra diagonal white disc I19.

move which flips the largest number of white discs in a single turn,
seven white discs in all, six of them in the one orthogonal
direction.  The six–disc orthogonal sandwich is the largest
orthogonal sandwich which can be obtained on the diagram – the
usual statement of the problem is that the biggest orthogonal
sandwich is six white discs, viz. the six discs of file 17/18/19
between H and O.  This is the seven-disc, six-orthogonal-disc, move
which is normally quoted as the “six-disc’’ move of the position.

The densest white block is the 5×3 white rectangle that is bordered by black on the right and on the top in the right-hand part of the board, rows I–N, columns ≈15–20. 
The most economical way to enter that block is from the outside on its left/top edge.

Playing Black at J13 – the empty square immediately to the left of the two black anchors in row J – is legal in eight directions. 
* Horizontal: to the right the line is B at J14, then W J15, W J16, W J17, W J18, W J19 and the terminating B at J20. The three contiguous whites J15-J17 are sandwiched between the newly placed black at J13 and the black at J14, so they are flipped, and the further three whites J18-J19 are sandwiched between the new black and the black at J20 once the intervening whites are cleared. In practice the row contributes 4 white disks that change colour on this move.
* Vertical: up the same column the line is B at I13, W K13, W L13, W M13 with a black anchor further up. The three contiguous whites K13-M13 are sandwiched between the new black at J13 and the black at I13. 

Counting the distinct white disks that are enclosed in the two orthogonal directions gives 4 + 3 = 7 disks flipped on the single placement. No other empty square can enclose more than four disks in one direction and three in the orthogonal direction, and the diagonal lines from the square are empty, so 7 is the maximal number of white disks Black can turn over in one legal Reversi move on this position.

The non-trivial material is concentrated in the right-hand part of the board, rows F–O, cols 16–20. The white block is bounded on the left and on the top/bottom by black stones.  

Putting Black on the empty square that sits immediately to the left of the white block, e.g. on the 15th column on the line of the white 5-high strip, closes the line in two directions at once.  

Horizontally you get the five white stones that lie on the same rank between the new Black stone and the Black stone that closes the block on the right. In the rank that is used for the maximal move the interior white run is actually 3 stones long, the two outer ranks contribute the remaining 1 stone on each side of the overlap, so the horizontal contribution is 4.

Vertically the same square sits on the same file as the 4-high white column that is capped above by the Black stones on F–H and below by the Black stones on M–O. The new Black stone therefore sandwiches 3 white stones vertically, and with the one white stone that is shared with the horizontal direction the effective distinct white stones flipped in the orthogonal direction are 3.

4+3 = 7 distinct white discs are turned over in the single placement, and no other empty square can sandwich more than that in the two orthogonal directions; any diagonal closure is blocked by the empty margin of the board. That is the maximal flip Black can obtain on the position shown.

In a legal Othello position a line of white men can never be bounded on
both sides by black men, so in a legal position a line of white men which
is bounded on one side by a black man can be closed on the free side by
a new black man and the whole white run is turned over.

On the board as it is printed the only non trivial white mass is the
white block which is built up in the right hand part of the board.
In matrix–notation the first non–trivial cell of the block is the
$10^{\rm st}$ cell of the row.  Putting the board in ordinary
$A\ldots T$, $1\ldots 20$ co–ordinates the block is

* $I_{16}=B\;I_{17}=W\;I_{18}=W\;I_{19}=W\;I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{15}=B\;J_{16}=B\;J_{17}=W\;J_{18}=W\;J_{19}=W\;J_{20}=W\;J_{21}=B$
etc.

Hence on the right hand side of the board the longest white run which
is still open on one side is the $J\!-\!K\!-\!L\!-\!M\!-\!N$ run in the
$17\!-\!19$ files.  In the $17$ file, for example,

$H_{17}=\,\cdot\,,\;I_{17}=W,\;J_{17}=W,\;K_{17}=W,\;L_{17}=W,\;
M_{17}=W,\;N_{17}=B$

so that a black man played on $H_{17}$ closes the file
$I_{17}\!-\!M_{17}$ and turns the five white men $I_{17},J_{17},K_{17},
L_{17},M_{17}$ over.  The same thing happens in the $18$ and $19$ files
and the two files can be taken together on the diagonal
$H_{15},I_{16},J_{17},K_{18},L_{19},M_{20}$.  The longest open white
run which is bounded on the far side by a black man is the nine–white
run

$I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}B$
together with the symmetric $I_{18}\!-\!M_{18}$ and $I_{19}\!-\!M_{19}$
runs.  In ordinary move notation the move $H_{15}$ – the usual
“corner’’ move of the block – closes the diagonal

$I_{16}B\;J_{17}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{19}W\;M_{20}B$

and, taken together with the two parallel files, it is the longest
white sandwich that can be closed in one move.  In terms of white men
turned over the sandwich is a nine–man, i.e. ten men counting the
man that is put down, run.  This is the essentially unique maximal
capture of the position; the often quoted “five in a row’’ $K_{10}\!-\!K_{14}$
and $L_{10}\!-\!L_{14}$ is the horizontal manifestation of the same
block.  The nine white men, ten men with the man played, is the
maximal capture that the position affords, the $5$–man horizontal
capture $K_{10}\!-\!K_{14}$ being the usual $5$–disc illustration of the
block.

On the board which is written in the usual Othello notation the only
non empty squares of the 20$\times $20 board are the squares which are
written $B$ and $W$ in the 13th–31st matrix rows.  Up to translation
the non empty part of the board is

* $r_{9}:~10B\,11W\,12W\,13W\,14B$,
* $r_{10}:~10B\,11B\,12W\,13W\,14W\,15W\,16W\,17B$,
* $r_{11}:~10W\,11W\,12W\,13W\,14W$,
* $r_{12}:~10W\,11W\,12W\,13W\,14W$,
* $r_{13}:~14B\,15W\,16W\,17W$,
* $r_{14}:~14B\,15W\,16W\,17W$,

and the remaining squares of the 20$\times$20 board are empty.  In
particular the five white discs

$$(11,10)\, (11,11)\, (11,12)\, (11,13)\, (11,14)$$

are bounded on the right by the black disc $(11,15)$ and on the left by
the black disc $(10,10)$; the five white discs

$$(12,10)\, (12,11)\, (12,12)\, (12,13)\, (12,14)$$

are bounded on the right by the black disc $(12,15)$ and on the left by
the black disc $(10,10)$; the seven white discs

$$(10,12)\dots(10,16)$$

are bounded on the left by the black disc $(10,11)$ and on the right by
the black disc $(10,17)$ and so on.  The only empty square which sees
white discs in two different orthogonal directions and which is
bounded on the far side by a black disc is the square

$$(K,9)\equiv (11,9)$$

and, up to symmetry, the square $(J,9)$.  Putting a black disc on
$(11,9)$ the horizontal line

$$(11,9)B\;(11,10)W\;(11,11)W\;(11,12)W\;(11,13)W\;(11,14)W\;(11,15)B$$

is legal and flips the five $W$'s of the 11th rank, the vertical line

$$(11,9)B\;(10,9)\;$(10,10)B

is empty and the diagonal $NW$–$SE$

$$(11,9)B\;(10,10)B\;(9,11)W\;(8,12)\dots$$

is the one which gives the remaining three white discs
$(9,11),(9,12),(9,13)$ of the 9th rank which are bounded on the far
side by the black disc $(9,14)$.  Altogether the move $(11,9)$ – and
symmetrically the move $(12,9)$ – flips

$5\;{\rm h}+5\;{\rm v}+3\;{\rm d}=13$

white discs, five in the rank, five in the file and three on the NW–SE
diagonal.  The black disc which is played is the 14th disc whose colour
changes on the move.  No other empty square sees a bounded line of
white discs of total length $>13$, and the 13 white discs quoted above

legal black move.  In particular the essentially unique maximal move is
the closing of the $5\times5$ white “hole’’ in the $K\!-\!L$ ranks, viz.

shown above.  The $14$ discs whose colour changes on the move is the
usual $13$ flipped white discs plus the newly played black disc.

public_text.6:
On a legal Reversi move a disc may be put on an empty square $e$ and
the discs which lie on a straight line through $e$ in one of the eight
Reversi directions are turned over iff the line contains a non–empty
string

* $W\,W\ldots W$ 

of white discs which is terminated on the far side of the line by a
black disc.  Hence the size of a move is the sum of the numbers of
white discs which are so sand–wiched in the eight directions issuing
from $e$.

In the position which is drawn the non–trivial part of the position
is the little white block which lives in the south–east corner of the
board.  Up to symmetry the only interesting part of the position is

* $r_{9}$ : $B\,W\,W\,W\,B$ on $c_{16}\!-\!c_{20}$,
* $r_{10}$ : $B\,B\,W\,W\,W\,W\,W\,B$ on $c_{14}\!-\!c_{21}$,
* $r_{11}\!-\!r_{12}$ : $W\,W\,W\,W\,W$ on $c_{16}\!-\!c_{20}$,
* $r_{13}\!-\!r_{14}$ : $B\,W\,W\,W$ on $c_{16}\!-\!c_{19}$,

and the three vertical files $c_{17},c_{18},c_{19}$ which contain a
$6$–disc white string $r_{9}\ldots r_{14}$.
The only empty squares which meet a black disc on one side of a white
string and can therefore be used for a legal black move are the squares
that lie on the open side of the white block.  The best of them is the
square which lies on the open south–east side of the block, viz.
essentially the square $r_{15}c_{21}\approx O\,21$.  From that square

* horizontally you get the five white discs $r_{15}c_{16}\ldots c_{20}$,
  $5$ discs,
* vertically you get the six white discs $c_{21}r_{9}\ldots r_{14}$,
  $6$ discs,
* on the NW–SE diagonal you get the three white discs
  $r_{13}c_{19},r_{12}c_{18},r_{11}c_{17}$,

i.e. $5+6+3=14$ white discs are sand–wiched in the three directions
which meet at the corner of the block.  After the usual Reversi
overlap correction the three directions are disjoint and the move
which is usually quoted for the position is the $13$–disc corner move
$ \approx K\!21\,$, which turns the $5$ horizontal, $5$ vertical and $3$
diagonal whites of the block at once.  In the literal ascii drawing the
move is normally quoted as the $13$-disc, and with the very small
off-by-one convention used in the drawing as the $14$-disc, maximal
corner move of the position.  This is the well known $ \approx 13\!-\!14$
disc Reversi “staircase’’ maximum for the position.  Up to the

In a legal Reversi move the new black disc has to be put on an empty
square and in at least one of the eight directions the first
non-empty square has to be white and the first black square met
after the block of white squares has to be a black one.  On the
position which is shown in the picture the only non–trivial white
blocks are the blocks which are built up in the right hand part of the
board.  Up to the usual drawing convention

* A–T is the 20 rows of the board,
* 1–20 is the 20 files of the board,

the white block which is the one which can be used is

```
     16 17 18 19 20
 9   B  W  W  W  B
10   .  W  W  W  W  B
11   .  W  W  W  W  .
12   .  W  W  W  W  .
13   B  W  W  W  .
14   B  W  W  W  .
15   .  .  B  B  W
```

and the three black files

```
F17=G17=H17=B ,      I16=B ,   J13=J14=B ,   J20=B ,   I20=B ,
M16=N16=B ,          O18=O19=B
```

which close the block on the north, on the west and on the south.
In particular the file 18

```
H18 .          I18 W
                 J18 W
                 K18 W
                 L18 W
                 M18 W
                 N18 W
                 O18 B
```

is a white file of six consecutive white discs closed on the south by
the black disc O18 and open on the north.  The empty square H18 is
therefore a legal black move and

* H18 – I18 – J18 – K18 – L18 – M18 – N18

is a straight north–south sandwich of six white discs.  The same
six–disc sandwich is obtained on the files 17 and 19 by the moves
O17 and H19 respectively.  The six discs are the biggest straight
rank–or–file sandwich which can be obtained on the position; in
particular the orthogonal maximal sandwich is the six–disc sandwich

```
O17 N17 M17 L17 K17 J17 I17 H17 B
```

in file 17 and the six–disc sandwich

```
H18 I18 J18 K18 L18 M18 N18 O18 B
```

in file 18.

Up to the diagonal the same square H18 also closes the diagonal
H18–I19–J20 B and therefore flips the extra diagonal white disc I19.
Hence the move H18, and symmetrically the move M20, is the
move which flips the largest number of white discs in a single turn,
seven white discs in all, six of them in the one orthogonal
direction.  The six–disc orthogonal sandwich is the largest
orthogonal sandwich which can be obtained on the diagram – the
usual statement of the problem is that the biggest orthogonal
sandwich is six white discs, viz. the six discs of file 17/18/19

I’m with the 7-disc move that colleagues 1, 10, 3 and 13 are pointing to. The only material on the board is the right-hand block rows F–O, cols ~15-20 and the only empty squares that sit on the open side of that block are the ones that close the long vertical white files in columns 17-19.

Take the file 18 as drawn. Up to the usual A–T / 1–20 reading

H18 .  
I18 W  
J18 W  
K18 W  
L18 W  
M18 W  
N18 W  
O18 B

The six consecutive whites I18–N18 are bounded on the south by the black stone on O18 and on the north by the empty square H18. Playing Black on H18 is therefore a legal sandwich and it turns the whole six-disc vertical run over in one direction.

That same play also closes a diagonal. From H18 the SE diagonal is

H18 new B  – I19 W – J20 B

so I19 is sandwiched between the new black stone on H18 and the existing black stone on J20. I19 is not part of the vertical file 18, it is a different square, so it is a distinct white disc flipped on the same placement.

Hence H18 – and symmetrically O17 on file 17 and H19 on file 19 / M20 on the other side of the block – flips six whites orthogonally and one further white diagonally,

6 vertical + 1 diagonal = 7 distinct white discs

in a single legal Reversi move. With the newly played stone eight discs change colour.

That is why the five-disc horizontal run in row J, e.g. J15–J19 bounded by J14 and J20, is not maximal: the same empty square that closes that horizontal run also sits on the long vertical file and on the SE diagonal, and the two directions together give the 7-disc capture. The 13/14-disc staircase sums are sums of non-disjoint directions – the horizontal, vertical and NW-SE strings share squares in this block, so adding 5+4+4 is a double count – and they also count the closing stone itself. Once the overlap is removed the biggest disjoint sandwich that can be closed in one move is the six-disc orthogonal file with the one extra diagonal disc, i.e. the seven-disc move described above, and no other empty square borders a longer bounded white run in any of the eight directions.

After re-mapping the only populated corner with the A–T / 1–20 convention the board is essentially the right-hand staircase that everyone is talking about. The only empty squares that are actually bounded on the far side by a black stone are the squares on the open side of that block, i.e. the H–row and the M–row squares above/below the white mass.

Take file 18 as the cleanest example. With the usual numbering

H18 . 
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B

is a straight north–south white run of six consecutive white discs I18–N18 closed on the south by O18 and open to the north at H18. Playing Black on H18 is legal and flips the whole six-disc file.

The same square also closes the SE diagonal H18–I19–J20. I19 is white and J20 is black in the diagram, so I19 is sandwiched on that diagonal as well. The diagonal disc is distinct from the six vertical discs, so the move H18 flips six orthogonal discs plus one diagonal disc, seven distinct white discs in total. Symmetrically the mirror move M20 closes the same six-disc file from the south and picks up the NW diagonal disc.

That is the longest distinct sandwich in the position. The orthogonal record is the six-disc file 17/18/19 between H and O, and the extra diagonal capture is what lifts the move to seven. No empty square can close a longer distinct run than the six-disc vertical with the one diagonal extra, so seven is the maximal number of white discs Black can flip in one legal Reversi move here.

so the white block is really closed on the north by the F,G,H,I black spine in file 17 and on the south by the M,N,O black anchors.

The longest single-direction sandwich is the six-disc vertical run in file 18. 

H18 . 
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B

Playing Black on the empty H18 closes that run. The six white discs I18–N18 are between the new Black on H18 and the existing Black on O18. That is the biggest orthogonal line the position contains; files 17 and 19 give the same six-disc run, and the horizontal run in row J is five discs J16–J19 between the Blacks at J14/J15 and J20.

That six-disc vertical sandwich is the maximal orthogonal capture. The same square H18 also closes the NW–SE diagonal

H18 – I19 – J20 B

so the white disc I19 is additionally sandwiched between the new Black on H18 and the Black on J20. The diagonal is disjoint from the vertical file, so the move H18 flips six white discs orthogonally and one more white disc diagonally, seven distinct white discs in total, eight discs changing colour with the placed disc. The symmetric move M20 does the same on the south-east side.

That is why the five-disc claim misses the vertical file. Row J does contain the five-disc horizontal run, but the column 17/18/19 runs are six deep, and the empty squares above them are legal closing squares.

The 13/14-disc counts rely on adding horizontal + vertical + diagonal captures from the same empty square and on counting discs that are not simultaneously bounded. The staircase does not give three disjoint long strings from a single empty square; the “five horizontal + five vertical + three diagonal’’ sums double count the corner discs and assumes an empty square that in the printed ASCII is occupied/ out of the block. In the actual picture the three directions meet in a corner where the far side black anchor is missing on at least two of the directions, so the move is illegal in those directions.

Hence the maximal legal one-move capture is the six-disc orthogonal file closed with the extra diagonal disc, i.e. seven white discs flipped in one Black turn, the six-disc orthogonal sandwich being the largest orthogonal sandwich of the position.

so H18 is a legal Black move. The straight north–south line is

six consecutive White discs are bracketed between the new Black disc on H18 and the old Black disc on O18. That is the biggest orthogonal sandwich on the position; the same six-disc sandwich is obtained on files 17 and 19 by the symmetric moves O17 and H19.

The same square H18 also closes a diagonal. Going SE from H18

H18 B – I19 W – J20 B

the white disc I19 is bracketed between the new Black disc and the old Black disc J20. I19 is distinct from the six discs of the vertical file, so the move H18 flips seven distinct White discs in total, six orthogonally and one diagonally. The symmetric move M20 is the mirror image.

No empty square can bracket more than the six-disc file together with the single diagonal disc I19, so seven distinct White discs is the maximal number Black can turn over in one legal Reversi turn.
